# Local MCP and verification contract

The MCP adapter manages the same Compose, native, and mixed runtimes as the CLI.
Policy-controlled container commands and automated browser verification require
Compose services. Named HTTP endpoints also support native applications.

## Start the server

For project setup in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, or Gemini CLI,
use the [agent setup helper](https://github.com/fugatolabs/fugato/blob/main/docs/guides/agent-setup.md). It installs the workflow
skill, adds persistent project instructions, and registers a stdio launcher that
starts the local daemon on demand. The release archives include the helper and
skill alongside both binaries.

Install the binaries using the [install guide](https://github.com/fugatolabs/fugato/blob/main/docs/guides/install.md). When
building from source, run `go build -o fugato-mcp ./cmd/fugato-mcp` from
`packages/fugato`. For a direct MCP binary launch, run `fugato ls` first; it starts
the daemon on demand without starting workloads. Then configure the client to
launch `fugato-mcp` with:

```text
FUGATO_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:46655
FUGATO_API_TOKEN_FILE=<state directory>/token
```

Run `fugato setup --agent cursor --project /path/to/project` to install the
workflow skill and project-scoped MCP configuration. The generated
`.fugato-agent/mcp-launch.sh` starts the daemon via the installed CLI before
launching the stdio server, keeping stdout reserved for MCP messages. Other
supported agents use the same setup command with their profile name.

The state directory is the daemon's `FUGATO_STATE_DIR`, or the operating system's user config directory plus `fugato`. The token file must be user-only. The server writes only JSON-RPC frames to stdout and uses the MCP `2025-11-25` stdio lifecycle. It supports `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`.

The MCP process reloads the token file for each daemon request. If the daemon
state directory is replaced while an MCP session remains open, the next request
uses the new token; a rejected mutation is never retried automatically. The
file must remain a regular user-only file (mode `0600`), and a symlink is
rejected. An unauthorized response identifies a mismatch between the API URL,
token file, and running daemon without printing the token.

Run `sh .fugato-agent/mcp-launch.sh --check` to start the local daemon if needed and verify
that the installed MCP binary can make a read-only daemon request. The check
prints its result to stderr and exits without starting an MCP session. A direct
binary launch also supports `fugato-mcp --check` when the two environment
variables above are set. Setup does not start the daemon; run this check explicitly after installation.

## Tools

| Tool | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_runtimes` | none | `{runtimes: [...]}` |
| `get_runtime`, `start_runtime`, `stop_runtime`, `get_preview_url` | `runtime_id` | runtime record |
| `get_logs` | `runtime_id`, optional `lines` (1–200) | bounded text, truncation flag, runtime record |
| `prepare_worktree` | `path`, `from`, optional `dry_run` | preparation report with paths and statuses |
| `run_command` | `runtime_id`, `service`, `argv`, optional `timeout_ms` | exit code and bounded output, runtime record |
| `verify_http`, `verify_browser` | `runtime_id`, optional `endpoint`, relative URL `path`, and `timeout_ms` | structured verification report |

Runtime records contain the worktree and project paths and the current Git
commit when available. If Git metadata cannot be read, `commit` is empty and
`metadata_error` explains the failure separately from runtime state.

Runtime operations require an existing explicit runtime ID. Register the project
without starting workloads using `fugato create --worktree PATH`, then use
`start_runtime`; `fugato up --worktree PATH` registers and starts in one step.
The MCP server never selects a worktree from its own process directory.
`prepare_worktree` uses explicit source and target paths instead of a runtime ID.
`stop_runtime` retains project data. HTTP/browser verification uses declared named
endpoints; supply `endpoint` when multiple eligible endpoints exist.
`get_preview_url` returns a URL only when the running runtime has exactly one
browser endpoint. For multiple endpoints, inspect their URLs through the CLI's
`fugato ports` command or the editor.

`prepare_worktree` is available before runtime registration and does not take a
runtime ID. Supply absolute `path` and `from` project directories explicitly;
the target must already exist, and both projects must be in the same Git
repository. It uses the target project's declared preparation inputs, preserves
existing destination files, and returns the same bounded path/status report as
the CLI. A blocked preflight returns a structured report with an error. This
operation uses authenticated daemon control and shared bounded metadata
admission; it does not start workloads or retry automatically.

`run_command` is denied unless the daemon state directory contains a user-only `command-policy.json` file. It maps runtime IDs to exact allowed argv sequences for selected Compose services:

```json
{"version":1,"runtimes":{"0123456789abcdef":{"web":[["node","--version"]]}}}
```

Use the actual ID from `list_runtimes`. The file must have mode `0600` and is reloaded for each call. Project branches cannot change this policy. The Compose adapter invokes the selected service container without a shell, adds an in-container `timeout` command, and caps stdout and stderr at 64 KiB each. The image must provide `timeout`. The maximum requested duration is 30 seconds. Relative `dir` is reserved in the API contract but not supported by this Compose adapter.

## Daemon API

The MCP adapter calls the daemon's loopback-only, bearer-authenticated `/v1/agent/runtimes` endpoints. This separate path preserves the current CLI response shape. The Go `control.Service` interface in `packages/fugato/internal/control/contract.go` defines the API boundary. The daemon's `ControlService` maps it to the runtime manager; backend-specific command and browser execution remain explicit extension points.

The browser worker is bundled in `packages/fugato/internal/verify/browser.cjs`. The Compose runner launches it with `--no-deps` in the project's selected `browser.service`, using its configured or inferred profile. Browser verification reports an unconfigured capability when no service is selected. Each call creates and closes a new Playwright browser context. The report includes status, page errors, failed requests, HTTP failures, screenshot path, and bounded relevant logs. Screenshots are stored under the daemon state directory with user-only permissions. They have no automatic expiry and survive runtime destruction; see the [cleanup guide](local-resources.md). A browser context isolates browser state; the runtime backend supplies the execution boundary.

## Backend integration checklist

The Compose backend provides registry lookup, start/stop, scoped command execution, and the Playwright browser service. Project images used for Compose command execution must provide `timeout`; the policy file remains user-owned outside the worktree. A later backend would implement the same interfaces if a concrete requirement warrants it.

Protocol references: [MCP stdio transport](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports) and [MCP tool results](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools).
